chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ṣaffār, from al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ṭāṭarī, from Ibn Ribāṭ, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There come out from the urethra al-manī, al-madhy, al-wady, and al-wadhy. As for al-manī, it is that for which the bones become relaxed and the body becomes languid from it, and in it there is ghusl. As for al-madhy, it comes out from desire and there is nothing due in it. As for al-wady, it is that which comes out after urination. And as for al-wadhy, it is that which comes out from illnesses, so there is nothing due in it.

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةِ: sexual desire, identified here as the cause of al-madhy
key_terms.الْأَدْوَاءِ: illnesses or ailments, identified here as the cause of al-wadhy
key_terms.الْإِحْلِيلِ: the urethra, the passage from which these fluids exit
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath made obligatory by the emission of al-manī
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid discharged due to desire, with no ruling due here
key_terms.الْمَنِيُّ: semen; the discharge that necessitates ghusl
key_terms.الْوَدْيُ: a discharge that comes out after urination

ai.seo_question: Which bodily discharges require ghusl according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the different fluids that may exit from the urethra and distinguishes their legal rulings. It states that only al-manī necessitates ghusl, while al-madhy and al-wadhy do not entail anything, and it defines each fluid by its cause or accompanying sign.
